# Persistence migration fixtures

`container-scene-v2.sketchyup` is the actual R014 package acceptance wall-ring
save, written by the R012 schema-v2/container-v2 implementation. Its document ID
is `bb542e3223382cc3380b8bb8c1c9bb6a` and revision is 1. Raw v2 contains the same
payload; raw v1 removes revision and later transform/property fields, matching the
original experimental schema. All geometry is the project's own room recipe.

R015 must read these without source mutation, allocate deterministic initial edge
IDs, and preserve those edge records across the current schema roundtrip.

`container-curves-v4.sketchyup` was captured from commit `25594d6` with the
project's `examples/curves.json` recipe before adding guide support. It has five
curve contexts (circle, center arc, two-point arc, three-point arc and pie).
`raw-curves-v4.json` is its unmodified document chunk. R027 must preserve its
analytic records and topology while initializing an empty guide collection.

`formline-v1.formline` is an original synthetic fixture for R037: a rotated box,
a hidden cylinder whose unused depth differs from its diameter, and a small box.
Its format follows the prototype validator/renderer inspected on 2026-10-03; no
prototype runtime or original scene was restored.

`m4-complete-v11.sketchyup` is generated by
`build/dev/m4_persistence_tests --write-fixture tests/fixtures/m4-complete-v11.sketchyup`.
It contains nested groups, two shared component placements (including a mirrored
nonuniform transform), an unplaced definition, tags, hidden/locked state, analytic
curves, guides, properties, front/back materials, present/missing assets and retired
ID allocation floors. The test compares every serialized record after relocation
and edits a canonical component member after reopening. It is original synthetic
project data under the application license.

`model-style-v17.sketchyup` is unmodified schema-17 writer output from the installed
R062.b build (PR #135, commit `3662b9e`), using `examples/model-style.json`.
It contains a monochrome cube with nondefault model style. R063 migration adds
only an empty saved-scene table, allocator 1 and the new schema version; geometry,
style, resource records and document identity/revision must remain exact.

`display-precision-v25.sketchyup` is generated by
`build/dev/display_precision_io_tests --write-fixture tests/fixtures/display-precision-v25.sketchyup`
(R084.r). It contains one 1 ft × 2 ft face in a feet-and-inches model at a display
precision of two decimal places. The test requires exact re-encoding and that every
older fixture migrates to Full precision. It is original synthetic project data.

`instances-v24.sketchyup` is unmodified schema-24 writer output from commit
`8534bb67` (main before R082.cc), generated by
`build/dev/instanced_storage_tests --write-fixture tests/fixtures/instances-v24.sketchyup`.
It stores the expanded member bodies of nine placements of three definitions:
shared, hidden, tagged, locked/mirrored with properties, a nested assembly and its
second placement, and a make-unique sibling. R082.cc migration must rebuild every
member from its definition with identical IDs, records and allocator floors, and
must reject a corrupted member by name without changing the file.

`instances-v25.sketchyup` is unmodified schema-25 writer output from commit
`44eca11e` (main after R084.r display precision, before R082.cc's schema 26),
generated by the same `instanced_storage_tests --write-fixture` builder. It holds the
same nine expanded placements at Full display precision. It must migrate exactly to
schema 26 and pass the same member projection check as the v24 fixture.

`release-1.0.0-v26.sketchyup` is unmodified schema-26 writer output from the released
SketchyUp 1.0.0 (tag `v1.0.0`, commit `7b01bb7a`), retained by R090.b before schema 27
(ADR 0163). The tag was checked out in a detached worktree and its CLI built with
`cmake --preset headless -DSKETCHYUP_BUILD_CLI=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF` and
`cmake --build build/headless -j6 --target sketchyup-cli`; from that worktree,
`build/headless/sketchyup-cli --script examples/saved-scenes.json --output release-1.0.0-v26.sketchyup`
wrote the file (writer `SketchyUp/1.0.0`, document `b3ff7415893e3ca1b3cc3ccafd507a52`,
revision 1). It holds one extruded box and two saved scenes. Every later build must
read it exactly, migrate it with empty drawing-sheet tables, and keep writing its
sheet-free content as schema 26 that the 1.0.0 reader accepts.

`drawing-sheets-v27.sketchyup` is generated by
`build/dev/drawing_sheet_io_tests --write-fixture tests/fixtures/drawing-sheets-v27.sketchyup`
(R090.b). It holds a face, two saved scenes, two drawing sheets in nondefault order
with a retired third sheet, and three views: a technical-lines view with an accepted
stamp, a raster-appearance view without one, and a view whose scene was deleted (a
broken link). Its sheet and view allocators are above the live IDs. R091.b regenerated
it while schema 27 was still unreleased (ADR 0163 decision 6): the plans sheet has a
number and a nondefault margin, and the sheets hold nine page items covering every
kind, orientation, alignment, dash style and label target, in a nondefault z order,
with a retired item ID and a dimension whose anchor body was deleted. R091.g regenerated
it again, still before release: the plans sheet has a nondefault dimension format (feet
and inches, 2 decimals, unit shown). The test requires
exact re-encoding apart from the writer string, and package acceptance requires the
prior package to refuse it unchanged. It is original synthetic project data.

`release-1.1.0-v27.sketchyup` is unmodified schema-27 writer output from the released
SketchyUp 1.1.0 (tag `v1.1.0`, commit `093484f9`), retained by R093.c before schema 28
(ADR 0165 §5). It was written by the published package
`sketchyup-1.1.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` (SHA-256
`e718b8fb0e52bb5ec40b6817b99c92a824242f4a20907a02f50f47e3f0c0d00a`), installed with
`pacman -U` in a throwaway `archlinux:base-devel` container (image
`sha256:061679925e5d5028f2df9395d441ce6c4b9accf0157ff3486c06b6962e014ef1`), by
`sketchyup-cli --migrate-native input-drawing-sheets-v27.sketchyup --output release-1.1.0-v27.sketchyup`,
where the input was a copy of `drawing-sheets-v27.sketchyup` as it stands at `v1.1.0`
(writer `SketchyUp/1.1.0`, document `a70aaf3e3f7cbb7a90579b5bf3a335a7`, revision 30,
SHA-256 `e3e037a06e283c90e3c8de5a58e4f452f640b295f7f654436f7c5cfca400143d`). It holds
the same face, saved scenes, two drawing sheets, three views and nine page items as
that fixture. Every later build must read it exactly, load it with empty component
parameter tables, and keep writing its parameter-free content as schema 27 that the
1.1.0 reader accepts.

`component-parameters-v28.sketchyup` is generated by
`build/dev/component_parameter_io_tests --write-fixture tests/fixtures/component-parameters-v28.sketchyup`
(R093.c) from `makeTable()` in `tests/component_parameter_fixture.hpp`. It holds the
ADR 0165 §1 table: parameters of every type (with bounds, a step and choice options)
and both modes, one driver of every kind with a retired driver ID below the allocator,
a room assembly that nests one table and drives its width through `childParameter` and
whose placement overrides it, a table at its defaults, and a table that overrides
width, shelves and finish, so two repeat copies are bound. The test requires the
records to equal the builder's and exact re-encoding apart from the writer string, and
the prior release must refuse it unchanged. It is original synthetic project data.

`terrain-dem-v34.sketchyup` is a schema-34 document with a GeoTIFF terrain (R107.b1). It is written by
`build/dev/terrain_import_tests --write-fixture tests/fixtures/terrain-dem-v34.sketchyup`, which runs
`sketchyup-cli --import-terrain` on the synthetic `geotiff/plane-f32-strip-none-le.tif` as USGS 3DEP:
a 300 m square window in UTM zone 30N, referenced to NAVD88. The terrain carries its source record in
`provenance.dem`. `terrain_io_tests` requires this build to read the file and write it back bit for
bit, and the 1.5.x reader to open it unchanged (the 1.4.x reader refused it). It is original synthetic data
(`geotiff/make_geotiff_fixtures.py`).

`reference-geo-v35.sketchyup` is a schema-35 document with a georeferenced reference image (R107.b2.1). It is written by
`build/dev/sketchyup-cli --import-reference-image tests/fixtures/reference/north-up.png --reference-zone 30N --output
tests/fixtures/reference-geo-v35.sketchyup`: the synthetic 8 by 6 PNG and its world file, in UTM zone 30N, which also
sets a site origin with its geographic record (so the file carries `geographic-site-v1` too). `native_format_tests`
requires this build to read the file and write it back bit for bit, and to refuse a file that names an unknown
required feature. The published 1.5.0-1 reader refuses it and leaves it unchanged: `--validate-native` exits with
status 1 and prints `{"code":"INVALID_OPERATION","error":"Invalid required features","status":"failed"}` (checked on the
package, 2026-10-31). `native_format_tests` runs that check when `SKETCHYUP_PRIOR_CLI` names the reader. It is original
synthetic data.

`reference/` holds the synthetic orthophoto fixtures for the R107.b2.1 reader and importer, written by
`reference/make_reference_fixtures.py` (run with `python3 -I`; `north-up.jpg` needs `cjpeg`). They are 8 by 6
pixels in UTM zone 30N unless their names say otherwise: PNG and JPEG with world files, 8-bit RGB and RGBA GeoTIFFs
(strips, tiles, LZW, Deflate, predictor 2, big-endian, pixel-is-point, NAD83 UTM 10N, UTM 56S, a
ModelTransformation), and one file per refusal (`refuse-ortho-*.tif`, `refuse-rotated.png`, `not-tiff.tif`).
No downloaded imagery is in the repository.
